resourceName: National REDD+ Project in the Democratic Republic of Congo
description:
National REDD+ Project in the Democratic Republic of Congo is a unique REDD+ project proceeding with mitigation of climate change, biodiversity loss, and habitat destruction along with an objective of enhancing the livelihood of the communities in the provinces of Tshopo, Sankuru, Tshuapa, Equateur, Bas-Uele and Maniema. This project is basically a community based REDD+ project with no evictions, no conflicts involved and without any displacement of human settlements. The project aims at conservation of 72,010,950 hectares of project area including several endemic, endangered, threatened species and their critical habitat. The Project has obtained all relevant formal written approvals of different levels from the National Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development Kinshasa, such as homologation certificates, attestation identification certificates, conformity certificates, environmental clearance certificate, harmonized CN REDD+ certificates including a ruling on the sharing of carbon credits income among the stakeholders. 

Project’s climate benefits include emissions (avoided) of approximately 1,559,409,567 tCO2e per annum and 155,243,885,277 tCO2e during 100 years of project lifetime. The project progresses on substantial co-benefits with Climate, Community, and Biodiversity performing at VERRA VCS CCB triple gold level. The project will have positive impact on the well-being of hundreds of thousands of people with enhanced awareness of natural resources, improved health care and education facilities, clean drinking water, enhanced food security & livelihoods and there by leading to more stability and tranquillity in the region.  Biodiversity co-benefits achieved through enhanced protection of the habitat through regular monitoring and patrolling of the forest areas will have a notable positive impact on our planet’s biodiversity.
